text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture as Aston Villa host Crystal Palace at Villa Park.
Aston Villa have endured a mixed start to 2023-24, recording two wins and two losses prior to the international break.

Unai Emery's team – who have been tipped to compete for European qualification again after reaching the Europa Conference League last season – were beaten 3-0 at Liverpool last time out, but they are a different proposition at Villa Park.
They have won their last eight league matches on this ground in a run dating back to February, only conceding twice in those games.
Crystal Palace are one point clear of Villa, with a 3-2 victory over Wolves taking them to seven points from their first four matches of the Premier League season before the international break.

Roy Hodgson's team have yet to lose on the road this term – they could go unbeaten through their first three away games of a league campaign for the first time since doing so as a second-tier side in 2003-04.
Villa's line-up shows just one change from the team that was beaten at Anfield last time out, with Diego Carlos ruled out through injury.
Galatasaray loanee Zaniolo comes in for his first start for the club, meaning Cash returns to right-back after playing a more advanced role against Liverpool.
Crystal Palace have confirmed Hodgson was taken unwell earlier today, so he is not present at Villa Park.
Hodgson is in contact with Paddy McCarthy and Ray Lewington, who will take charge in the manager's absence – our best wishes are with him.
Palace make two enforced changes with defender Marc Guehi and midfielder Jefferson Lerma out injured, bringing in Richards and Hughes.
Villa are looking to avoid losing successive Premier League games for just the third time since Emery took charge last year.
Will they bounce back from their defeat to Liverpool? The teams are out, and we're about to find out!
Following a minute's silence to remember the victims of the recent earthquake in Morocco, we are under way at Villa Park.
Eze with the first touch.
Palace look to attack down the right early on, but Digne shepherds the ball back to Martinez, who clears.
Villa then win a free-kick on halfway.
Kamara fouls Hughes as Palace win a free-kick just inside Villa's half.
The visitors – donning their white and sky blue change kit – are stoking the ball around nicely in the opening minutes.
Cash and Diaby are involved as Villa work possession from right to left and back again, but Palace are standing firm with 11 men behind the ball.
Doucoure then makes a strong challenge to prevent Watkins from shooting from the edge of the area.
Palace have scored just five goals in 11 Premier League away games against Villa (0.45 per game), never netting more than once in a match on this ground in the competition.
Only at Tottenham (0.36) do they have a lower away goals-per-game ratio against sides they've faced 10 or more times.
It's a nervous moment for Palace as Diaby latches onto a pass down the right before cutting back to Watkins, but the striker is crowded out and Cash is unable to divert the loose ball goalwards.
Edouard then has space to break, but Villa recover to win possession back.
Kamara releases Diaby with a wonderful ball over the top, but Richards matches the former Bayer Leverkusen man for pace before sliding in to divert his cutback back to Johnstone.
Now Palace come forward as Eze twists away from Douglas Luiz, but the Brazilian sticks to his task to force the Palace playmaker back.
If the visitors are to build on their promising start to the season here, Eze will surely have a big role to play.
England international Eze completed more dribbles (13) and created more chances from set plays (seven) than any other player in the Premier League across the season's first four matchdays.
He will be Palace's dangerman again here.
Villa want a foul as Watkins goes down, but the referee waves play on.
Luiz steps in to thwart a Palace break before getting the hosts moving forward again.
Villa are the team looking to ask questions of their opponents here.
Cash scampers down the right before offloading to Luiz, who sees his cross blocked by Schlupp.
Palace are proving a tough nut for Villa to crack here, sitting deep and looking to keep things tight.
Palace win possession and look to break through Eze, who is barged over by McGinn.
He becomes the first player to see yellow in this game.
Eze also goes into the book for waving an imaginary card at the referee after being felled.
HUGE CHANCE! Villa should be 1-0 up as Watkins is played clean through on goal.
He looks to bend his finish into the bottom-right corner, but Johnstone gets down to make a vital one-on-one save.
Villa attack again, and Richards almost turns Cash's low cross into his own net, slicing behind for a corner.
Nothing comes of the Villa corner, but they keep the pressure on.
Palace eventually scramble it clear before the referee stops the game for Ayew to receive treatment following a clash with McGinn.
Ayew is okay to continue after receiving treatment, as Palace get the game back under way through a drop-ball for Johnstone.
Zaniolo charges into the box before looking to cut back from the left, but Richards is there to make a strong block.
Cash turns inside before sending a tame shot straight at Johnstone, then the game is stopped again as Ayew drops back to the turf.
The forward has tried to continue, but his game looks to be done.
Ayew is unable to shake off his injury and is replaced by Mateta.
That switch could see Edouard move out to the right flank.

With a hat-trick against Plymouth Argyle in the EFL Cup and two assists from the bench against Wolves last time out, Mateta has been involved in as many goals in 109 minutes across his last two games in all competitions as he was in his previous 44 appearances for Crystal Palace.
Can the substitute make an impact here?
Andersen prevents Watkins breaking in behind with a crucial defensive header.
Eze then gets Palace moving and feeds Edouard, but the forward's cross is blocked before rebounding off him and behind for a Villa goal-kick.
Palace are growing into this game now.
The ball is worked out to Eze on the left corner of the box, but his dangerous cross just drifts behind with no Eagles team-mate attacking it at the far post.
Luiz is hacked down by Doucoure, who is perhaps fortunate to avoid a booking.
Digne lines up a deep free-kick from the left flank, but he sends an awful cross straight into the wall.
We're past the half-hour mark at Villa Park, and this game is very much in the balance.
Watkins has missed the best chance of the match, but Palace are starting to look a little more dangerous on the break.
Villa work the ball out from the back nicely with Luiz and Torres involved.
Palace recover possession and come forward again, but Eze overhits his pass towards Mateta.

GOOOOOOAAAAAAL! DIABY PUTS VILLA AHEAD! Torres' pass over the top of the Palace backline finds Diaby, who takes an outstanding first touch before slotting his finish into the bottom-right corner! But wait... there will be a VAR check here – Diaby may have been offside!
NO GOAL! Palace breathe a sigh of relief as the VAR review finds Diaby was fractionally ahead of Richards when the pass was played.
That's such a shame for Villa, who see a fine opening goal chalked off.
The score remains 0-0.
Close! Cash flashes a low cross into the six-yard box, but Watkins is on his heels and can't reach it as Palace escape.
That disallowed goal appears to have sparked Villa into life!
TWO CHANCES FOR CASH! How are Villa not ahead? Cash miskicks when left unmarked 10 yards out, but Villa keep the pressure on through Digne.
He whips a fine cross to the far post, where Cash is completely free but can only head over the crossbar!
Now Zaniolo gets to the byline before seeing his cutback cleared.
The pressure is growing on that Palace backline.
A rare forward foray from Palace sees Edouard attempt to link up with Schlupp, but he completely miscues his backheeled pass and Villa recover possession.
Eze goes for goal from 20 yards out, but Konsa is there to deflect it wide for a Palace corner.
Eze initially stays down, having been caught by a heavy challenge as he lined up the shot, but he's soon back to his feet and able to take the corner.
Eze's corner is cleared at the near post.
The visitors have been under pressure and they need to make more of those situations.
Villa have lost just one of their 11 previous Premier League home games against Palace (W6 D4), going down 1-0 in December 2013.
We will have five minutes of additional time before the break.
The earlier stoppage for Ayew's injury accounts for much of that.
Great defending from Richards! Watkins almost latches onto a pass into the box on the left side, but the defender gets across to make a vital interception.
Zaniolo goes into the book, having thrown the ball away to delay the restart after Palace were awarded a throw-in.
The Italian thought the decision was going to go his way.
Digne plays a menacing cross into the area from the left, but nobody is there to attack it for Villa.
They keep the attack alive, and Diaby sees a shot charged down on the edge of the area.
Villa are appealing for a penalty, claiming Diaby's shot hit Richards' outstretched arm inside the box.
It did strike his hand, but he had his back to the ball.
No penalty!
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-0 CRYSTAL PALACE.
It's still goalless between Aston Villa and Crystal Palace as we reach the interval.
The hosts have certainly shown more endeavour, and they thought they were ahead when Diaby raced through on goal to slot home, only to be denied by an offside call.
Johnstone was called into action by Watkins earlier in the half, while Cash should have done better with a free header.
Palace have shown next to nothing in attack – there is surely more to come from them.
Villa have managed seven shots to Palace's one, creating 0.78 expected goals in that opening 45 minutes.
However, they have only hit the target once.
Will they end up regretting their missed chances?
Villa get the second half under way, with no changes for either side.
Will we get a winner?
Palace scored all three of their goals after the break when they beat Wolves last time out.
Since Hodgson returned to the club in April, they have scored a higher proportion of their goals after half-time than any other Premier League team (74 per cent, 17/23, minimum five goals).
The travelling fans will be hoping for more of the same here.

GOOOOOAAAAAAALLLL! EDOUARD PUTS PALACE 1-0 UP! The Eagles make a flying start to the second half! Mateta does brilliantly in the build-up, spinning Torres on halfway before charging down the right to find Edouard with a perfect pass into the centre.
Martinez slips as he looks to come off his line, allowing the Palace striker to side-foot home!
Torres will be disappointed after being shrugged off the ball too easily, but what a piece of play from Mateta.
He gets the assist following some fine work.
ALMOST 2-0! Edouard rides two challenges with a powerful run into the box, but Konsa and Torres just do enough to crowd him out as he looks to finish past Martinez.
Villa need to wake up!
Villa look to respond, but Digne's cross from the left is easily claimed by Johnstone.
What a start to the second half this has been for Palace, who offered very little in attack before the break.
Close again! Eze feeds Schlupp on the left, and his teasing low cross is just claimed by Martinez.
Edouard and Mateta were both lurking in search of a tap-in.
Hughes goes into the book following a clumsy challenge on McGinn.
The Palace midfielder is holding his knee, but he should be okay to continue.
Hughes clears a cross behind for a Villa corner, but Digne's poor delivery is headed away by Andersen.
Villa come again on the opposite flank, and Mitchell concedes another corner.
Digne's second set-piece delivery is a better one, but goalscorer Edouard is back to clear ahead of Watkins.
Emery has seen enough, with Villa's first changes imminent.
Zaniolo sees a cutback intercepted by Doucoure, and that will be his final action.
Bailey replaces him on the Villa left.
Tielemans is also on, replacing Kamara in midfield.
Unlucky! Hughes does brilliantly to keep an overhit pass alive before stretching to cross.
Mateta is waiting to prod it home, but Martinez dives on the ball.
WHAT A TACKLE! Villa look destined to draw level as Diaby offloads to Watkins, but Doucoure flies in with an exceptional challenge to stop him from pulling the trigger.
Villa want a penalty, but there's no chance – Doucoure got the ball before colliding with team-mate Ward.
Doucoure was hurt by his collision with Ward.
He leaves the field for treatment as Palace soldier on with 10 men.
Diaby's cross from the right is behind Watkins, who twists his body to send an acrobatic header towards the far post, but Johnstone is able to claim it with Bailey lurking.
Palace are then returned to their full compliment as Doucoure comes back on.
Eze feeds Mitchell on the overlap, but the left-back's cross is cut out by Konsa.
Hughes immediately wins the ball back as Palace keep the pressure on – the home fans are growing frustrated now.
Brave goalkeeping! Johnstone launches a long pass over the top, which Eze attempts to reach.
He looks set to get there, but Martinez darts from his line to smother the loose ball – that was a vital intervention.
Tielemans shoots from the edge of the box, but a combination of Richards and Hughes blocks the effort at close quarters.
Palace are defending resolutely as they look to hold onto their 1-0 lead.
This match is opening up as we approach the final 20 minutes.
Villa are throwing men forward in search of a leveller, but Palace continue to threaten on the break.
GREAT CHANCE FOR 2-0! Mateta wins a corner on the right, which is lifted in by Eze.
Andersen pulls away at the far post to nod it across goal, and Ward somehow sends a diving header comfortably wide from six yards out.
That could have been the clincher!
Duran replaces McGinn in another attacking change for Villa.
Well held! Duran latches onto a knock-down on the edge of the box before volleying at goal, but his left-footed strike skips along the surface into the gloves of Johnstone.
Villa are starting to penalty Palace back.
Bailey sees a cross headed out by Andersen, before Digne just fails to keep Torres' lofted pass to the far post in play.
OFF THE POST! It's desperate stuff from Palace as Hughes throws himself in front of Bailey's shot.
It rebounds to Watkins, who bends an effort towards the top-right corner.
The ball bounces off the post before hitting Johnstone on the back of the head and dropping wide! How is it still 1-0?!
Johnstone has stayed down in the goalmouth, holding his calf.
He looks to be in some discomfort and former Manchester United goalkeeper Henderson is warming up on the touchline.
Johnstone is back up and will continue, for now.
Henderson retakes his place on the bench as Palace prepare to defend this corner from the Villa right.
Palace clear their lines and break through Eze, but he overruns it on the left flank as Villa win a throw-in.
Good save! Schlupp scoops a pass over the top for Eze, who looks to lift the ball beyond Martinez.
The Villa goalkeeper reacts well, however, springing up to tip away before claiming it at the second attempt.
Palace are starting to look menacing on the break again now.
Eze goes for goal from 25 yards out, but Martinez gets down well to hold it.
We're into the final five minutes of the 90, though there will be plenty of stoppage time after Johnstone went down injured a few minutes ago.
Can Villa salvage a result?
Cash goes into the book for a kick on Edouard.
Palace can eat up a few valuable seconds with a free-kick inside Villa's half.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLL! WHAT A STRIKE FROM DURAN! VILLA ARE LEVEL! Digne lifts his head up before floating a cross onto Duran's chest, just inside the penalty area.
The substitute takes it down before swivelling and firing a left-footed volley into the top-left corner! Villa have their equaliser, and what a strike it was!
Digne gets the assist, but Duran deserves all the credit for that wonderful finish.
The home fans are in fine voice now with Villa chasing a winner!
Ahamada replaces Edouard for Palace.
They might be content to escape Villa Park with a draw now.
Duran tries to reach a long ball into the box but catches Richards on the top of the head with his studs.
That was brave defending from Richards, who really threw himself into that battle.
We will have at least NINE additional minutes here! Richards is back up and okay to continue for Palace, who restart the game with a free-kick in their own box.
Diaby darts to the byline before cutting the ball back, but Andersen is there to clear.
Palace are being pushed back now – Villa are the team in the ascendency.
PENALTY TO VILLA! Tielemans slides a lovely ball in behind for Watkins, who is bearing down on goal when he is brought down by Richards.
The referee points to the spot, but there will be a VAR check here – Richards might have got a touch on the ball before colliding with Watkins.
Darren England has been sent to the pitchside monitor to review the decision! This could be bad news for Villa...

THE PENALTY STANDS! Wow – late drama at Villa Park! Richards appeared to get a touch on the ball with his sliding challenge, but after a long review at the pitchside monitor, Darren England sticks with his original decision!
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAALLLL! DOUGLAS LUIZ SURELY WINS IT FOR VILLA! The Brazilian stutters in his run-up before sending Johnstone the wrong way, caressing the kick into the bottom-left corner.
Villa have snatched victory from the jaws of defeat.
Ward is booked for dissent following Villa's goal.
Now it's Palace desperately looking to carve out one last chance! They will feel hard done by following the award of that penalty.
There should still be plenty more stoppage time to play!
Rak-Sakyi replaces Doucoure as Palace try to respond.
Villa also make a change, with Dendoncker on for Watkins as they bid to hold on.

GOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAL! BAILEY KILLS OFF THE CONTEST! Villa wrap up the points following a devastating counter-attack, with Diaby reaching the byline before cutting back from the left for Bailey to steer in the third! What a remarkable finish we've had here at Villa Park! 3-1 to Emery's side!
Diaby gets the assist following some outstanding work, breaking down the left before putting it on a plate for opposite winger Bailey!
We're into the 104th minute and still playing here.
Villa Park is absolutely bouncing following that late double salvo from the hosts, who are about to leapfrog Palace in the Premier League table.
Bailey is shown a yellow card for wasting time towards the end of this clash.
Duran joins Bailey in the referee's book soon after, seemingly for a needless tactical foul stopping proceedings.
That should be that at Villa Park, though.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 3-1 CRYSTAL PALACE.
And breathe! It's full-time at Villa Park, and Aston Villa take the spoils after scoring three late goals to break Crystal Palace's hearts in a 3-1 triumph.
The Eagles went ahead through Edouard's finish on the break, and they still led with just three minutes of the 90 remaining.
However, Villa substitute Duran levelled with a ferocious volley before the award of a contentious penalty allowed Luiz to put Villa ahead deep into stoppage time.
With Palace chasing the game, Bailey turned in Diaby's cross to add a late third for the hosts.
What a win for Emery's men!
Palace will be absolutely gutted by the nature of that defeat.
They drop to eighth with seven points from five matches, with Villa jumping to seventh with nine points.

The Eagles are next in action against Fulham next Saturday, while Villa can turn their attentions to the Europa Conference League, with Legia Warszawa their opponents as they begin their group-stage campaign on Thursday.
We hope you've enjoyed our coverage of a remarkable fixture from the Premier League.
It's goodbye from us, and we'll catch you next time!
